premises.text: Stores use opaque dynamic pricing while price-drop guarantees are too complex and time-consuming for consumers to claim, so money owed goes unclaimed
premises.evidence_span: it's a huge hassle. Not only are the policies often complex by design, it takes a ton of time to price compare

premises.text: Paribus scans inbox receipts (OAuth), tracks prices/coupons, checks store policies, and uses NLP to automatically file price-adjustment claims
premises.evidence_span: It scans your inbox for receipts, tracks the prices on what you bought, and when they drop, automatically files claims to get you paid

premises.text: Receipts are pulled via subject/sender webhooks without reading other email contents, with bank-level security on stored data
premises.evidence_span: We placed customized webhooks to pull receipts and store communications based on subject and sender alone, without ever touching the contents of your other emails

premises.text: Paribus takes 25% of money saved (reducible to zero via referrals) and only earns after the user is paid
premises.evidence_span: Our standard fee is charged 25% of the money we earn you

value.text: Consumers effortlessly recover money owed when prices drop after purchase
value.evidence_span: Paribus is a web app that gets you the money you're owed effortlessly

causal_links.evidence_span: online consumers are leaving $10 billion on the table every year
The only time that Paribus earns is after we save you money first

notes: Dynamic pricing and guarantee hassle folded as one consumer-refund problem (§4.1.6). Inbox scan, account linking, scraping/coupons, policy DB, and NLP filing folded as one automation mechanism (§4.1.7); privacy/security kept as separately emphasized trust condition in product domain. Store-count and beta savings treated as traction. Anti-template: problem, product/privacy, and fee model separately revisable.
